title: A protocol for extracting immunolabeled murine cardiomyocytes of high-quality RNA by laser capture microdissection
protocol: Dissect mouse hearts using sterile forceps and small, sharp scissors.
Cut chest skin to expose the heart.
Use bigger scissors to cut the thoracic cage.
Sever arteries and veins connected to the heart.
Dissect the heart out carefully.
Transfer the heart to a Petri dish containing 1× PBS.
Wash the heart several times with fresh PBS using individually wrapped transfer pipettes.
Dispose of the carcass using labeled biohazard bags.
Fill half of an embedding cryomold with OCT slowly and carefully.
Cut the excised heart into two transverse sections using disposable scalpels.
Orient each individual section on the floor of one embedding cryomold pre-filled with OCT.
Fill the rest of the cryomold slowly with OCT, avoiding creation of bubbles.
Quickly and carefully lower the tissue in the cryomold into liquid nitrogen so it is partially submerged and sitting just on top of the liquid nitrogen.
Place the frozen tissue into −80°C freezer for storage after the OCT becomes solid white (∼10–15 s).
Spray RNaseZap™ on the PEN slide and leave for 5 min.
Wash the PEN slide with DEPC water.
Expose the slides to UV light for 30 minutes.
Label and keep the UV-treated slides face up at room temperature.
Set the cryochamber temperature of the cryostat to −22°C.
Set the specimen temperature on the cryostat to −20°C.
Clean the cryostat, microtome blade, and tools with 70% ETOH.
Wipe dry after cleaning.
Set the section thickness on the cryostat to 8 μm.
If cutting a new tissue block, set the cryostat to trim 20 μm thick sections until the whole tissue is exposed.
Adjust the thickness to 8 μm for further sections.
Remove the tissue block from the cryomold and mount it on the chuck using OCT.
Place the tissue/chuck assembly in the cryostat chamber and allow equilibration for 15 minutes.
Secure the chuck in the chuck stage of the cryostat.
Carefully bring the specimen very close to the blade.
Brush away tissue trimmings with paintbrushes.
Slowly cut and tease the tissue section away from the blade using paintbrushes.
Gently unroll the cut section using the paint brushes.
Pivot the PEN slide (membrane side facing the tissue section) slowly on top of the section.
Carefully remove mounted tissue from the chuck using a razor blade.
Transfer the tissue back to the cryomold.
Wrap the cryomold with aluminum foil.
Keep on dry ice until storage in -80°C freezer.
Store collected sections on PEN slides individually in 50 ml Falcon tubes containing silica desiccant beads.
Store Falcon tubes in -80°C freezer.
Allow stored Falcon tubes to equilibrate to 25°C completely before opening the lid.
Immunolabel murine cardiac sections with WGA and DAPI.
Select cardiomyocytes for microdissection using LMD.
Catapult selected cardiomyocytes into AdhesiveCap 500 opaque collection tube.
Fix sections in 100% acetone on ice for 5 min.
Use a PAP Pen to outline membrane area and prevent spread of solutions.
Pipette 500 μL PBS-RNAsecure™ on the section and decant after 30 s, repeat twice.
Incubate sections with primary antibody cocktail for 5 min.
Decant the antibody, pipette 500 μL PBS-RNAsecure™ on the section and incubate for 30 s, repeat twice.
Dehydrate sections by sequentially dipping the slide into 50 mL of 50%, 75%, 95%, 100% ETOH for 30 s each.
Remove RVC from dissected materials before performing downstream procedures such as reverse transcription and PCR.
Assess the accuracy of visualizing individual cardiomyocytes in cardiac sections using histochemical staining with Cresyl violet or hematoxylin and eosin.
Inspect stained sections under brightfield light microscopy for 5 minutes.
Wear gloves throughout the entire Laser Capture Microdissection procedure.
Switch on the computer, microscope, and laser 5 minutes before starting LMD.
Launch PALM RoboSoftware and wait for the stage to calibrate.
Load the PEN slide into one of the 3 slide holders by pushing the metal bar to the left.
Release the metal bar slowly to lock the slide in place securely.
Slot the tube cap into the horseshoe and pin back the tube.
Click “Capture Device” which opens the PALM RoboMover then PALM CapMover II window.
Select Collector type: TUBE 2 × 500 CMII on the PALM RoboMover.
Choose position (1) or (2) according to which tube position was chosen.
From the “Display” menu, choose “Camera” and select the installed camera from the drop-down menu.
Move the PEN slide to a section-free area using the Joystick.
Select “White Balance” on the screen.
Move back to the tissue section area.
Choose “Reflected Light” from the “Microscope” menu and select 5× objective lens.
Select “Focus” then select channels for inspection of fluorescently immunolabeled cells.
Activate or deactivate the fluorescence beam by opening or closing the fluorescence shutter, respectively.
Capture and save the image displayed on the screen at any time during LMD by clicking “Save Current Image”.
Click “Calibration” from the main menu.
Select “Cut Laser Adjustment Wizard” from the drop-down menu.
Proceed with rough laser adjustments.
Position the cursor precisely over the center of the marker hole to set the laser marker.
Calibrate the alignment and position of the laser marker with respect to stage movement.
Select the “Multi-Dimensional Acquisition” icon from the toolbar.
Create or modify multi-dimensional acquisition experiments from the drop-down menu.
Enter parameters of the dyes (Texas Red™ and DAPI) and exposure times for each fluorescence channel used.
Save the experiment by clicking on the icon again to start an experiment.
Optimize laser cut settings in a non-precious area of the slide before moving to areas of interest.
Select “MicroBeam” from the “Laser” menu to adjust laser settings.
Set laser CUT Energy: 38 and Focus 60 for cardiac tissue sections.
Set laser LPC Energy: 23 and Focus 5 for cardiac tissue sections.
Adjust the laser speed to 8–10 μm/s.
Draw a line around cardiomyocytes or cells of interest using freehand drawing tool.
Select “RoboLPC” cutting function and click “Start Cutting Laser” to cut and catapult the cell or area of interest.
Select “Oneclick-LPC” if the cell/area was partially catapulted and click inside the cell/area outline to fully catapult it.
Monitor laser cutting of all selected elements during the whole LMD procedure.
Click “Go to Cap Check” regularly to check the cap.
Change to the lowest magnification (5×) to visualize the largest area possible of the cap.
Move the stage to reach an empty area in the cap if elements start to accumulate.
Click “Capture Device”, choose “Adjust” option, click “Save Position as delta position for the collector”.
Click “Close”.
Move the stage back to the point of origin (cutting position).
Click “Element List”, choose the “Summary” sheet then click “Print” to save summary of total elements collected.
Once enough material has been collected, click “Capture Device”, click on “Home” to return the tube holder to start position.
Mount a new microfuge tube on the tube holder.
Microdissect 1 mm² tissue chunks from the same section.
Proceed directly with cell lysis for microdissected tissue chunks.
Proceed directly with cell lysis for captured cardiomyocytes.
Add 350 μL Buffer RLT containing 2-Mercaptoethanol to the tube containing 1 mm² tissue chunks.
Incubate the tube in an upside-down position at 25°C for 30 minutes.
Spin down the lysate in a microcentrifuge for 5 minutes at no more than 8,500×g at 25°C.
Store the tube on ice until RNA isolation is performed.
Perform the rest of RNA isolation steps according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dispense 7 μL of RNase-free water on the column’s filter and centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Dispense another 7 μL of RNase-free water and centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Pipette the eluted 14 μL on the column’s filter and centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 1 minute.
Assess the quality and concentration of 1 μL of the isolated RNA using Bioanalyzer and Agilent RNA 6000 Pico kit.
Store the remaining RNA at −80°C.
Prepare the Cells-to-CT lysate after all cardiomyocytes are captured by LMD.
Dispense 50 μl of lysis reaction on top of the microdissected cardiomyocytes in the AdhesiveCap, pipette up and down several times for 1 min.
Incubate the lysis reaction mix upside down for 5 min at room temperature.
Spin down the lysate and add 5 μL Stop Solution to the lysis reaction, pipette up and down five times and incubate for 2 min at room temperature.
Store the lysate on ice for ≤2 h or at −20°C to −80°C for ≤5 months.
Prepare an RT Master Mix in a nuclease-free microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Mix the RT Master Mix gently but thoroughly, then spin down and place on ice.
Incubate the RT mix at 37°C for 30 min then 95°C for 5 min.
Store assembled RT reactions at 4°C for up to 4 hours.
Prepare the PCR Cocktail according to the Recommended final concentration of each primer (200–400 nM).
Distribute the PCR Cocktail into individual PCR tubes or wells of a real-time PCR plate.
Pipette cDNA up and down slowly 4-5 times.
Add 6 μL cDNA to 14 μL PCR Cocktail.
Close the PCR tubes or cover the plate.
Mix gently.
Spin down the tube contents to remove bubbles and collect the contents at the bottom of the wells.
Set up the real-time PCR instrument as indicated in the table.
Load and run the reactions.
